observations: Photo 0: Close-up of control panel showing text 'PSR-540', 'FLOPPY DISK DRIVE' label, dust/grime on casing, and a row of yellowed keys.
Photo 1: Wider view of keyboard with green LCD screen lit but showing no clear menu text, several blue and red buttons, pitch/modulation wheel area, yellowed keys.
Photo 2: Close-up of the gold pitch bend/modulation wheel, screen, and a black speaker grille on the right side of the unit.
Only one speaker grille is visible across all three photos; the other side of the unit is not shown.
No photos of the back panel, power adapter, battery compartment, or full front/side view of the casing.
Screen shows a uniform green glow without visible text or icons, could indicate backlight only or a demo screen.

claims.claim: It's a used YAMAHA PSR 540 with first body
claims.evidence: Model text 'PSR-540' is visible in photo 0, but 'Yamaha' branding and 'first body' (original, non-replaced casing) claim cannot be confirmed from the photos; no logo or serial plate shown.
The gold pitch bend wheel is visible in photos 1 and 2, but no video or demonstration shows it moving or affecting sound.
Only one speaker grille is visible (photo 2, right side); the second speaker is not shown in any photo.
Photo 1 shows a green-lit screen with no visible text, numbers, or icons, so screen legibility and backlight evenness cannot be confirmed.

risks.risk: Pitch bend wheel may be loose, unresponsive, or not affecting pitch as claimed
risks.proof: Short video showing the wheel being moved while a note is held, demonstrating audible pitch change

risks.risk: Screen may have dead pixels, dim backlight, or failed segments despite being lit
risks.proof: Clear daylight photo of the screen displaying a normal menu or voice selection screen

risks.risk: Second speaker may be missing, damaged, or disconnected
risks.proof: Photo of the opposite side of the keyboard showing both speaker grilles, plus an audio/video clip of sound from both channels
risks.if_unproven: priced as single working speaker only

risks.risk: No power adapter shown; unit may be sold without one, increasing buyer cost
risks.proof: Photo of the power adapter/cable included in the sale

risks.risk: Casing or keys may have hidden cracks, missing buttons, or key sticking not visible in close-up shots
risks.proof: Full front, back, and side view photos of the entire keyboard body
risks.if_unproven: priced at visible cosmetic condition only, assuming possible hidden damage

risks.risk: Floppy disk drive (visible label in photo 0) may not function, common failure point on PSR-540 units
risks.proof: Video showing a floppy disk being read or saved successfully

proof_requests: Video of keyboard powering on, showing the main menu/screen clearly and demonstrating sound from both speakers
Video demonstrating pitch bend wheel in use with audible pitch change
Photo of the full keyboard body (front, back, both sides) to check for cracks or missing parts
Photo of the power adapter being used to power the unit
Photo/video showing the floppy disk drive reading a disk
response.reason: The model is identifiable as a Yamaha PSR-540 from photo 0, and the visible condition (dust, yellowed keys, unconfirmed screen and speaker function) allows pricing at worst-case assumptions for unverified functional claims.
